mainTopic: Which animals, parts and milks are included in the איסור of בשר בחלב, and whether one איסור can take effect on top of another.
overview: The גמרא finishes proving that the plain word גְּדִי ('kid') includes a calf and a lamb, so בשר בחלב applies to all kosher domesticated animals. The Torah adds 'of the goats' only where it means goats, and the גמרא defends this reading with the rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד and with two limiting words, עזים and העזים. Then שמואל reads each of the three mentions of 'גדי' and 'בחלב אמו' as including or excluding cases: fat, a dead animal, a fetus, blood, the placenta, non-kosher animals, and certain kinds of milk. The גמרא asks how three words can teach so much, and answers that some teachings share one word and others come from logic. Since that answer assumes שמואל holds אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר, the גמרא raises a contradiction from his teaching about a טמא כהן eating טמאה תרומה and gives three answers. רב then rules that milk from a female goat that has never nursed is forbidden, because she can become a mother. Finally, רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue whether one who cooks חלב in milk gets מלקות. The גמרא shows that the argument is about cooking, not eating, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Plain 'kid' includes a calf and a lamb
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק about יהודה says 'kid of the goats,' a plain גדי must include a cow and a ewe as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'a kid of the goats.' That shows that wherever the תורה says just 'kid,' even a calf or a lamb is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that the plain word גדי is not limited to goats. That matters for the איסור of בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If גדי by itself already meant a goat, the תורה would not need to add 'of the goats.' The extra word shows that plain גדי is broader. So the פסוק 'do not cook a גדי in its mother's milk' covers cattle and sheep too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is how we know that בשר בחלב applies to beef and lamb, not only to goat meat.

phrases.english: Here it says 'a kid of the goats,'
phrases.notes: This points back to the פסוק quoted just before, about יהודה sending a kid of the goats (בראשית 38:17).

phrases.aramaic: הָא כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר גְּדִי סְתָם –
phrases.english: so anywhere 'kid' is said plainly,
even a cow and a ewe are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן גְּדִי עִזִּים, הָא כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר גְּדִי סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation that began before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plain גדי includes a calf and a lamb, so בשר בחלב applies to all kosher domesticated animals.

steps.title: Why not learn the opposite from this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe this פסוק teaches that גדי always means a goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe the פסוק shows that every גדי means a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק could be read the other way. It might be explaining what גדי means, so we would apply 'goat' to every place the word appears, including בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn from it (and apply it elsewhere)

phrases.english: But let us learn from it?
phrases.notes: He means: learn from this פסוק that every 'kid' is a goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵילַף מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that plain גדי is broader than goats.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could just as easily be defining גדי as a goat, and that definition would apply everywhere.

steps.title: A second פסוק also adds 'of the goats'
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק, about רבקה and the goatskins, also says 'kids of the goats.' This shows the תורה has to spell out 'goats' each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another פסוק is written: 'And the skins of the kids of the goats.' Here it says 'kids of the goats,' so anywhere 'kid' is said plainly, even a cow and a ewe are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by bringing a second פסוק that also adds 'of the goats.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first פסוק had taught that every גדי is a goat, the second פסוק would not need to add 'of the goats' again. Since the תורה repeats it, adding 'goats' must be needed each time, so plain גדי is broader.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
'And the skins of the kids of the goats'
here it says 'kids of the goats,'
so anywhere 'kid' is said plainly,
even a cow and a ewe are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An additional פסוק shows that the first one is not a general definition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first פסוק defines גדי as a goat everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the תורה has to say 'goats' a second time, plain גדי is not limited to goats.

steps.title: Why not learn from the second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: let the second פסוק teach that גדי always means a goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge comes back, now aimed at the second פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק could be needed for its own story, and the second one could teach the general definition that גדי means a goat. So the answer in step 3 seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: But let us learn from it?
phrases.notes: Now 'it' means the second פסוק, about the goatskins.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵילַף מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of step 2 against the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the second פסוק to prove that plain גדי is broad.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second פסוק could itself be the source that defines גדי as a goat everywhere.

steps.title: Two פסוקים that teach the same thing
steps.stepSummary: Both פסוקים teach the same point, so under the rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד we cannot learn from them for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are two פסוקים that come as one, and any two פסוקים that come as one do not teach about other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a known rule: when two פסוקים teach the same idea, we do not apply that idea anywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה wanted the idea to apply everywhere, one פסוק would have been enough. Writing it twice signals that it is limited to these cases. So the meaning 'goat' stays only in those two places, and plain גדי elsewhere is broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Two פסוקים that teach the same point
They do not teach about other cases

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards: you would expect two פסוקים to make a point stronger. But the rule says the repetition shows the point is limited to those cases.

phrases.aramaic: הָווּ לְהוּ שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: They are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach about other cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָווּ לְהוּ שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule about how פסוקים are learned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second פסוק defines גדי as a goat everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both פסוקים say the same thing, so neither one teaches about other places.

steps.title: What about those who say two פסוקים do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The answer only works for the view that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד do not teach. What about the view that they do?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says they do not teach. But for the one who says they do teach, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last answer depends on a disputed rule and asks how the other side would explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about whether two פסוקים that teach the same point can be applied elsewhere. For the side that says they can, the two goat פסוקים should teach that every גדי is a goat, and the proof for בשר בחלב falls apart.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says they do not teach,
but for the one who says they do teach,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the answer in step 5 works for every view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer depends on a disputed rule, so it does not work for the other view.

steps.title: Two limiting words: עזים and העזים
steps.stepSummary: The two פסוקים contain two limiting words, עזים and העזים. These keep 'goat' limited to those places, even for the view that two פסוקים do teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two limiting words are written: 'goats' and 'the goats.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an answer that works for everyone: the words 'goats' in the two פסוקים act as limiting words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if two matching פסוקים could normally teach about other cases, here the תורה wrote 'goats' in one פסוק and 'the goats' in the other. These two מיעוטים tell us that only in these places does גדי mean a goat. So plain גדי, as in בשר בחלב, includes a calf and a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: Limiting words (words that narrow a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Plain גדי includes cattle and sheep, so בשר בחלב applies to all kosher domesticated animals. The תורה says 'goats' only where it means goats specifically, and those words limit the meaning to those places.

phrases.english: Two limiting words are written:
'goats' and 'the goats.'
phrases.notes: 'Goats' is from the פסוק about יהודה, and 'the goats' is from the פסוק about the goatskins.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי מִיעוּטֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 in a way that works for every view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to the exact wording: limiting words in the פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under the view that two matching פסוקים do teach, every גדי would mean a goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two limiting words keep 'goat' confined to these פסוקים, so plain גדי is broad for everyone.

steps.title: שמואל's list of what 'kid' and 'its mother's milk' include and exclude
steps.stepSummary: שמואל uses each of the three mentions of 'גדי' to include one case and exclude one case. He uses each of the three mentions of 'בחלב אמו' to exclude a kind of milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: 'גדי' includes forbidden fat. 'גדי' includes a dead animal. 'גדי' includes a fetus. 'גדי' excludes blood. 'גדי' excludes the placenta. 'גדי' excludes a non-kosher animal. 'In its mother's milk' excludes the milk of a male. 'In its mother's milk' excludes the milk of a slaughtered animal. 'In its mother's milk' excludes the milk of a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching from שמואל. He reads each repeated word in the פסוק about בשר בחלב as teaching something extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says 'do not cook a גדי in its mother's milk' three times. שמואל takes each 'גדי' as adding one case to the איסור and taking one case out. He takes each 'בחלב אמו' as taking one kind of milk out.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to add a case to the rule
To exclude; to take a case out of the rule
Forbidden animal fat (not the same as חָלָב, milk)
A fetus, an unborn calf or kid
The placenta, the sac that holds the fetus

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חֵלֶב (forbidden fat) with חָלָב (milk). In 'לרבות את החלב' שמואל means the forbidden fat. It is also counted as a 'גדי' that can be cooked in milk.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
'Kid' comes to include the forbidden fat;
phrases.notes: The תורה writes 'גדי' in milk three times: שמות 23:19, שמות 34:26, דברים 14:21.

phrases.english: 'kid' comes to include a dead animal;
'kid' comes to include the fetus.
'Kid' comes to exclude the blood;
'kid' comes to exclude the placenta;
'kid' comes to exclude the non-kosher animal.
'In its mother's milk', and not in the milk of a male;
phrases.notes: 'Mother' means female, so milk from a male animal, in the rare case it has some, does not count.

phrases.english: 'in its mother's milk', and not in the milk of a slaughtered animal;
'in its mother's milk', and not in the milk of a non-kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: ״גְּדִי״ – לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַחֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier discussion of whether 'גדי' means only a goat to a new teaching of שמואל about what the repeated words include and exclude.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three mentions of 'גדי' include fat, a dead animal and a fetus, and exclude blood, the placenta and a non-kosher animal. The three mentions of 'בחלב אמו' exclude the milk of a male, of a slaughtered animal and of a non-kosher animal.

steps.title: Three words cannot teach six rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that 'גדי' is written only three times, yet שמואל drew six teachings from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Kid' is written only three times, and we are expounding six things from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's count. Three words should give three teachings, not six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word in the תורה can normally teach one thing. שמואל used each 'גדי' twice, once to include and once to exclude. That looks like more teachings than there are words.

keyTerms.meaning: We expound, we learn out from the פסוק

phrases.english: But 'kid' is written three times,
and we are expounding six!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תְּלָתָא ״גְּדִי״ כְּתִיבִי, וַאֲנַן שִׁיתָּא דָּרְשִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count of teachings in שמואל's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's six teachings from the word 'גדי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are only three mentions of 'גדי', so there is not enough text to support six separate teachings.

steps.title: Some teachings share a word, some need no word, so two remain
steps.stepSummary: Fat and a dead animal come from one word, because שמואל holds אסור חל על אסור. Blood and the placenta do not need a word at all. That leaves two words: one for the fetus and one to exclude a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds that one איסור can take effect on top of another איסור, so the איסור of fat and of a dead animal come from one פסוק. Blood also is not a 'kid' at all, and the placenta is just a secretion. Two are left: one to include the fetus, and one to exclude a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by cutting the list of six down to the ones that really need their own word. It ends with exactly two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat and a dead animal are both already forbidden. So both teach one idea, that בשר בחלב still applies on top of another איסור, and one word is enough for both. Blood and the placenta are not meat, so they are left out by logic and need no word. Once those are removed, only the fetus and the non-kosher animal still need a word.

keyTerms.meaning: A second prohibition can take effect on something already forbidden
They are learned from one פסוק
A secretion, waste, not real meat

steps.whatToRemember: Only two of שמואל's six 'גדי' teachings need their own word: the fetus is included and a non-kosher animal is excluded. Fat and a dead animal share one word. Blood and the placenta are left out by plain logic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: when there seem to be too many teachings for the words, it sorts out which ones come from logic and which ones share one source.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: Shmuel holds that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיסּוּר חֵלֶב וּמֵתָה מֵחַד קְרָא נָפְקִי.
phrases.english: so the prohibition of fat and of a dead animal come from one verse.
Blood, too, is not a 'kid' at all,
and the placenta, too, is merely a secretion.
Two are left:
one to include the fetus,
and one to exclude a non-kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by showing that only two teachings truly need their own word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reducing the count: some teachings are combined into one source and others come from logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each of the six 'גדי' teachings needs its own word, which would mean six words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fat and a dead animal share one word. Blood and the placenta need no word. Two words remain, one for the fetus and one for the non-kosher animal.

steps.title: Does שמואל really hold that one prohibition can take hold on top of another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 10 from another teaching of שמואל. There he says a טמא כהן who eats טמאה תרומה is not punished with death, because that תרומה was already 'desecrated.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Does שמואל really hold אסור חל על אסור? But שמואל said in the name of רבי אלעזר: How do we know that a טמא כהן who ate טמאה תרומה is not punished with death? Because the פסוק says 'and die therein if they desecrate it.' That leaves out this תרומה, which was already desecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10, which said שמואל holds that a second prohibition can take hold on food that is already forbidden. It quotes a different teaching of שמואל that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טמאה תרומה is already forbidden to eat. If a second prohibition could still take hold, the טמא כהן would get the death penalty for eating it. Since שמואל says he does not, it looks like שמואל holds אין אסור חל על אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition takes hold on something that is already forbidden
A כהן who is ritually impure
תרומה that has become ritually impure
Punished with death by the hand of Heaven

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר?
phrases.english: And does שמואל hold that a prohibition takes hold on a prohibition?
But didn't שמואל say in the name of רבי אלעזר:
From where do we know that an impure כהן
who ate impure תרומה
is not punished with death?
As it says: 'And die therein if they desecrate it'
This excludes this one, which is already desecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption used in Step 10's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 10 that שמואל holds אסור חל על אסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere exempts a טמא כהן from death for eating טמאה תרומה, because it was already forbidden. That sounds like אין אסור חל על אסור.

steps.title: First answer: שמואל holds a second prohibition can take hold, but the תרומה case has a special exclusion
steps.stepSummary: In general, שמואל holds אסור חל על אסור. The תרומה case is different only because the פסוק 'ומתו בו' specially leaves it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: in general a prohibition does take hold on a prohibition. But there it is different, because the תורה limited it with 'ומתו בו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the idea that שמואל holds אסור חל על אסור. It explains the תרומה case as a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption for the טמא כהן does not come from a general rule. It comes from the extra words of the פסוק. So it tells us nothing about other cases, like meat and milk.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say:
In general, a prohibition takes hold on a prohibition,
and it is different there
because the Merciful One excluded it with 'and die therein.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּעָלְמָא אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the contradicting source to a special exception taught by a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תרומה case shows שמואל holds אין אסור חל על אסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תרומה case is a special exclusion from 'ומתו בו'; in general שמואל holds אסור חל על אסור.

steps.title: Second answer: שמואל holds a second prohibition cannot take hold, but meat and milk has a special inclusion
steps.stepSummary: The opposite approach: in general שמואל holds אין אסור חל על אסור. But in meat and milk the word 'גדי' specially includes fat and a dead animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: in general שמואל holds a prohibition does not take hold on a prohibition. But here it is different, because the תורה included it with 'גדי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the answer around. Now the general rule is that a second prohibition does not take hold, and the meat-and-milk case is the special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, one mention of 'גדי' was used to include fat and a dead animal. According to this answer, that inclusion is a special rule made by the פסוק, not a sign of שמואל's general view. So the תרומה teaching shows his real general view.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition does not take hold on something already forbidden
Kid (young goat); the word in the meat-and-milk פסוקים

phrases.english: If you want, say:
In general, שמואל holds
that a prohibition does not take hold on a prohibition,
and here it is different
because the Merciful One included it with 'kid.'
phrases.notes: This is the mention of 'גדי' that Step 10 used for fat and a dead animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּעָלְמָא קָסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, opposite answer to the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Treats the meat-and-milk case as the special exception, taught by a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 10 showed שמואל generally holds אסור חל על אסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל generally holds אין אסור חל על אסור; meat and milk is different because 'גדי' specially includes these cases.

steps.title: Third answer: one teaching is שמואל's own view, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: The meat-and-milk teaching is שמואל's own opinion. The תרומה teaching was said in the name of his teacher, רבי אלעזר, and reflects his teacher's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: this one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to solve the contradiction. The two teachings are not both שמואל's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה teaching was said 'in the name of רבי אלעזר.' So שמואל was only reporting his teacher's view that a second prohibition does not take hold. His own view, shown in meat and milk, is that it does.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers for שמואל: (1) he holds אסור חל על אסור, and תרומה is a special exclusion; (2) he holds אין אסור חל על אסור, and meat and milk is a special inclusion; (3) meat and milk is his own view, and תרומה is his teacher's view.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
This is his own, that is his teacher's.
phrases.notes: 'His teacher' is רבי אלעזר, in whose name שמואל said the תרומה teaching in Step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא דִידֵיהּ, הָא דְרַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different answer to the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two statements to two different people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both teachings are שמואל's own opinion, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat and milk is שמואל's own view; the תרומה teaching is רבי אלעזר's view.

steps.title: Cooking in the milk of a goat that has never nursed
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks רב: what is the law if someone cooks meat in the milk of a female goat that has not yet nursed a baby?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked רב: If someone cooks meat in the milk of a goat that has not nursed, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A student asks רב whether the milk of a female goat that never nursed counts as 'its mother's milk.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'בחלב אמו,' 'in its mother's milk.' This goat has milk but is not yet a mother. So maybe her milk is not included in the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question to settle a doubt)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי מֵרַב:
phrases.english: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked רב:
One who cooks meat in the milk of a goat
that has not nursed, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about which milk counts for meat and milk.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the milk of a female goat that has never nursed included in 'its mother's milk'?

steps.title: רב: It is forbidden, because she will become a mother
steps.stepSummary: רב proves from שמואל's teaching that only a male's milk is excluded. A female that has not nursed will become a mother, so her milk is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: Since שמואל needed to say that 'in its mother's milk' means 'and not in a male's milk,' we learn that only a male is excluded, because a male can never become a mother. But this goat, since she can become a mother, is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that cooking in this milk is forbidden. He brings a proof from שמואל's teaching in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל used 'בחלב אמו' to exclude a male's milk. רב reasons that he chose a male because a male can never be a mother. A female who has not nursed yet is a possible mother, so she stays included in 'its mother's milk.'

keyTerms.meaning: Into the category of a mother
From the fact that it was needed

steps.whatToRemember: Only a male's milk is excluded from meat and milk. A female's milk is forbidden even if she never nursed, because she can become a mother.

phrases.english: He said to him:
From the fact that שמואל needed to say
'in its mother's milk' — and not in a male's milk,

phrases.aramaic: זָכָר הוּא דְּלָא אָתֵי לִכְלַל אֵם,
phrases.english: it is a male that does not come into the category of a mother,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַאי, כֵּיוָן דְּבָא לִכְלַל אֵם
phrases.english: but this one, since she comes into the category of a mother,
is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּאִיצְטְרִיכָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden. שמואל only excluded a male's milk, which can never be a mother's milk; a female that has not nursed can become a mother.

steps.title: Argument: Is one flogged for cooking forbidden fat in milk?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue about whether someone who cooks חלב (forbidden fat) in milk gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone cooks forbidden fat in milk, רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue. One says he is flogged, and one says he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between two אמוראים about cooking forbidden fat (חלב) in milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב is already forbidden to eat on its own. The question is whether the איסור of meat and milk can still apply to it, so that the person gets מלקות. This fits right into the earlier discussion about whether one איסור can take effect on top of another.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal (not the same as חָלָב, milk)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up חֵלֶב (forbidden fat) with חָלָב (milk). The case is fat cooked in milk.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who cooks forbidden fat in milk:
phrases.notes: Watch the vowels: חֵלֶב is forbidden fat and חָלָב is milk.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi disagree:
one says: he is flogged,
and one says: he is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new אמוראי argument that connects to the earlier theme of אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר and to fat being included in meat and milk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether one who cooks חלב in milk gets מלקות.

steps.title: Suggestion: They argue about whether one prohibition can land on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument depends on the rule of אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they argue about this: the one who says he is flogged holds that one prohibition can take effect on another, and the one who says he is not flogged holds that one prohibition cannot take effect on another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out an explanation of what the two אמוראים are really arguing about. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will test the idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since חלב is already forbidden, the meat-and-milk איסור would have to land on top of an existing איסור. So it seems natural to link the argument to the big question of אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר. The word לֵימָא signals that this is only a suggestion, and it may be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (a suggested explanation that often gets rejected)
A prohibition takes effect on something already forbidden

phrases.english: Let us say that they disagree about this:
that the one who says he is flogged holds:
a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition,
and the one who says he is not flogged holds:
a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests the underlying reason for the מחלוקת in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the argument between רבי אמי and רבי אסי? Is it the rule of אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר?

steps.title: No: Everyone agrees about eating; the argument is about cooking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees אין איסור חל על איסור, so nobody is flogged for eating. They argue only about cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds that one prohibition does not take effect on another. About eating, everyone agrees he is not flogged. When they argue, it is about cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion from the last step and moves the argument to a different place: the act of cooking, not eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that the meat-and-milk איסור does not land on חלב for eating, because it is already forbidden to eat. So the מחלוקת cannot be about the general rule. It must be about whether you are flogged just for cooking the mixture.
steps.confusionAlert: The argument is not about eating the fat-and-milk mixture. Both sides agree there are no מלקות for eating. The argument is only about cooking.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees that
a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: אַאֲכִילָה דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא לָקֵי,
phrases.english: for eating, everyone agrees that he is not flogged,
when they disagree, it is about cooking.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18's suggestion and moves the argument from eating to cooking.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the מחלוקת depends on אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone actually holds אין איסור חל על איסור. The argument is only about cooking.

steps.title: Each side's reasoning about cooking
steps.stepSummary: One side says cooking is just one איסור, so he is flogged. The other side says the תורה wrote the eating ban using the word for cooking, which ties the two together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he is flogged holds that it is only one prohibition. The one who says he is not flogged holds that this is why the Merciful One expressed eating using the language of cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds the way he does about cooking חלב in milk. The second explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking חלב by itself is allowed. So the one who says לוקה holds that cooking it in milk breaks only one איסור (meat and milk), and no איסור is landing on another. The one who says אינו לוקה points out that the תורה wrote the eating ban using the word 'cook.' This ties cooking to eating, so cooking is not treated as a separate punishable act here.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the meat-and-milk איסור of cooking may depend on the איסור of eating. That decides whether there can be מלקות for cooking where eating is not punished.

phrases.english: The one who says he is flogged:
it is one prohibition,
phrases.notes: Cooking חלב by itself is allowed, so cooking it in milk breaks only the meat-and-milk איסור.

phrases.english: and the one who says he is not flogged:
for this reason the Merciful One expressed
eating in the language of cooking,
phrases.notes: The פסוק says 'לא תבשל גדי בחלב אמו' (שמות 23:19), and the גמרא finishes this thought right after.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר לוֹקֶה – חַד אִיסּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each side of the cooking argument that step 19 pointed to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning of each side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the argument must depend on אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether cooking is its own single איסור, or is tied to eating because the תורה used the language of cooking.
